_context: Global Layer 4 net — CreateProcessW hook in every injected process
_coverage: Any process spawned from an injected shell (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe)
Resolved exe path + args are visible post-parse — this is semantic-quality data
Tokens matched against BaseName(exe) so 'shutdown' matches C:\Windows\System32\shutdown.exe
Context-aware rules: an entry with "requiresFlag" only blocks when that flag is
present on the same command line. A single CreateProcessW call is one command +
its flags (no ';' / '|' ambiguity), so flag rules work here too. Example:
ping -t example.com     -> BLOCK   (-t = infinite ping, DoS / noise vector)
Flags are matched on literal text; '/' style switches (shutdown /s) and '-' style
(ping -t) are both recognized as flags. Abbreviations are NOT resolved.
BLIND SPOT: processes spawned outside an injected shell (injector has not yet targeted them)
DEMO PURPOSE: this is the only layer that sees an EXTERNAL BINARY launched from
PowerShell (e.g. `Start-Process shutdown` or `& taskkill.exe`) — the AMSI layer
(powershell-policy.json) inspects script/cmdlet content, not the resolved child
process, so external-binary invocations from PowerShell rely on THIS file.
The same tokens are also reachable from cmd.exe, so each rule below is
intentionally shell-agnostic and can be tested from both shells.

blocklist.reason: system shutdown or restart — blocked regardless of launching shell
destructive disk format — blocked regardless of launching shell
force-terminate processes — blocked regardless of launching shell
infinite ping (-t) — blocked regardless of launching shell
